PRESENT  THE HONOURABLE MR.JUSTICE P.G. AJITHKUMAR  Friday, the 15th day of March 2024 / 25th Phalguna, 1945  CRL.M.A NO.1/2023 IN CRLA 1352/2023  SC 472/2020 OF ADDITIONAL DISTRICT & SESSIONS COURT - I, KASARAGOD PETITIONER/APPELLANT/ACCUSED:
 XXXXXXXXXX RESPONDENT/RESPONDENT/COMPLAINANT:
 STATE OF KERALA REPRESENTED BY PUBLIC PROSECUTOR,HIGH COURT OF  KERALA, PIN - 682031  Application praying that in the circumstances stated therein the High Court be pleased to suspend the sentence imposed against the appellant in SC No. 472/2020 of Special Court for Atrocities against Women and Children (Additional Sessions Court-I), Kasaragod, for the proper adjudication of the case.

This Application coming on for orders upon perusing the application , and upon hearing the arguments of M/S. P.S.BINU, K.SEENA, S.RAJEEV,
Advocates for the petitioner and of the PUBLIC PROSECUTOR for the respondent,the court passed the following:
 P.G. AJITHKUMAR, J.
 ....................................
 Crl.M.A.No.1 of 2023  in  Crl.Appeal No.1352 of 2023  ..............................................................
 Dated this the 15th day of March, 2024  ORDER

This is a petition filed by the appellant under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Code).
2.
The petitioner would contend that he is innocent and there is every chance for allowing the appeal and acquitting him.
He was on bail during the trial of the case.
In such circumstances, he claims that he is entitled to get his sentence suspended.
3. The learned Public Prosecutor filed objection.

The petition is opposed by contending that the evidence adduced by the prosecution proved beyond doubt that the petitioner had committed the Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10734890/
1 offence alleged against him.
The offence proved against the petitioner is grievous.

On account of the offence he has committed and the consequent ostracisation, the victim, who was aged only 12 years,
has been put to untold miseries.
Considering the gravity and nature of the offence and the tenure of the sentence imposed, the petitioner is not entitled to get an order to suspend the sentence.
4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

5. The petitioner was convicted for the offence punishable under Section 377, 375(a) r/w 376(2)(n)
of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 5(l), (m) and (n) and (p) r/w Section 6, Section 9(l) and (m) r/w Section 10 and Section 11(iii) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO Act).

sentences.text: The term of sentence the petitioner has to undergo as per the impugned judgment is imprisonment for 15 years.
6. The charge leveled against the petitioner was as follows; the victim is the niece of the petitioner.

While she was studying in the 8th standard and on several occasions thereafter the petitioner had subjected her to penetrative sexual assault in the bed room on the first floor of the house belonging to her grand parents.
During the period, she was below the age of 12 years.
She was subjected to sexual assault on many occasions as well.
7. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that there have been serious discrepancies in the evidence of the victim and there is delay in launching the prosecution.
Therefore, the conviction is based on unreliable evidence, and the petitioner is entitled to get the sentence suspended.
I am unable to agree with the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the findings leading to conviction of the petitioner is wrong even prima facie.
8. The learned Public Prosecutor would submit that the evidence of the victim in so far as the sexual abuse by the petitioner is reliable despite she had changed her version during cross examination.
It was so happened since she was won over by the petitioner which is quite evident from the evidence came on record.
When the petitioner is none other than the uncle of the victim, there cannot be any leniency in the matter of suspension of the sentence.
9. PW1 is the victim.
I have gone through her deposition.
In the chief examination she had stated substantiating the charge leveled against the petitioner.
However, during cross examination, which was in a later day, she changed her version totally and she went even to the extend of denying that she was sexually abused by the petitioner.
When such contradictory statements were given before the court, credibility of the witness is at state.
Considering the relationship between the parties, the possibility of winning her over cannot be ruled out.
Whether evidence of PW1 can be placed reliance on especially in the absence of any independent evidence to render support, is a matter that requires deeper consideration.
I am of the view that in the circumstances of the case, although the offence is so serious, the execution of sentence is liable to be suspended subject to strict conditions.

10. Accordingly, this petition is allowed and the petitioner is granted bail on his executing a bond for Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees one lakh only), with two solvent sureties for the like amount each, to the satisfaction of the trial court, subject to the following conditions:
Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10734890/
2
(i) He shall deposit 50% of the fine amount to the trial court within one month.
(ii) He shall not enter the revenue district of Kasaragod till the final disposal of this appeal;
(iii) During the bail period, he shall not get involved in any offence; and (iv) He shall not contact or try to intimidate the victim or witnesses examined in the case.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to apply before this Court for cancellation of the suspension of sentence.

Sd/-
